JUDGMENT Heard Smt. Shruthi S.P. who represents Shri Vinaya Keerthy, learned counsel on record for the appellants as well as Shri Janardhana Reddy, learned counsel who is appearing for Respondent No.3 / Insurance Company.
2. This is a claimant's appeal challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Davanagere in MVC No.170/2012 dated 31.10.2014..
3. On this day, learned counsel who is representing the appellants files a memo stating that the first appellant is no more.

Having regard to the fact that no amount is awarded as compensation in favour of the first appellant, the request of the learned counsel for the appellant is considered for proceeding with the matter for disposal on merits.
Both the learned counsel further submit that the second appellant has attained the age of majority.
4. As per the material available on record, the deceased Sarala is the wife of the deceased first appellant NC: 2024:KHC:20984-DB and mother of the second appellant.
The said Sarala died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22.01.2012.

The Tribunal, through the impugned order,
awarded a sum of Rs.10,37,856/- as compensation in favour of the second appellant.

Raising a contention that the amount thus awarded is not in accordance with law and seeking enhancement,
the present appeal is preferred.

5. The limited question involved in this appeal is whether the Tribunal is justified in arriving at a conclusion that the second appellant is entitled to Rs.10,22,856/- under the head 'Loss of dependency' and Rs.15,000/- under other conventional heads.

As rightly projected, no amount is added towards 'future prospects'.
6.
It is not in dispute that the deceased Sarala was working as a Teacher in a private School and was drawing salary of Rs.15,042/- per month.
Equally, it is not in dispute that the deceased Sarala was aged about 35 years by the date of accident.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance NC: 2024:KHC:20984-DB Company Vs. Pranay Sethi and others (AIR 2017 SC 5157),, 40% of the actual earnings are required to be added towards 'future prospects'.

sentences.text: That apart, as rightly pointed out, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '16' and not '17' as applied by the Tribunal.

Therefore, re- calculating the figures, the amount of compensation that can be awarded under the head 'Loss of dependency' would be as under:
Monthly income Rs.15,042/-
Annual income Rs.1,80,504/-
Adding 40% towards future Rs.2,52,705.6/-
prospects Deducting 1/3rd towards Rs.1,68,470.4/-
personal expenses Applying appropriate multiplier Rs.26,95,526/-

sentences.text: Together with the said amount, the second appellant is entitled to Rs.70,000/- under conventional heads, i.e., 'Funeral expenses', 'Loss of Estate' and 'Loss of consortium'.

Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs.27,65,526/-
NC: 2024:KHC:20984-DB 8.
The Tribunal, through the impugned order, has awarded a sum of Rs.10,37,856/- as compensation.

Thus, the enhancement would be Rs.17,27,670/-.
9.

In the light of the foregoing discussion, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Davanagere, though orders in MVC No.170/2012 is enhanced by 17,27,670/-.
iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) The third respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
v) It is reported that the second respondent has attained the age of majority and proof to that effect is also produced before the concerned NC: 2024:KHC:20984-DB Tribunal.
The Tribunal is directed to re-verify and to disburse the amount to the second appellant, with due identification.
